responses: Max lit the brass lantern from the crate, and Bel nodded, saying they should go down. Bel then led the way into the tunnel with Max following, lantern raised.

messages.speaker: Max
messages.text: I pick up the brass lantern from the crate and light it.

messages.speaker: Bel
messages.text: Bel nods. "Then we go down." She leads the way into the tunnel.

messages.speaker: Max
messages.text: I follow Bel into the tunnel, lantern raised.

responses: At the counter, Ponticius offered two hundred gold for the Sun Ruins job, half upfront, and Max countered at three hundred. Ponticius settled on two fifty, and after Arin urged Max to accept since they needed the coin, Max agreed and took the pouch.

messages.speaker: Ponticius
messages.text: "Two hundred gold for the Sun Ruins. Half now, half when you bring back the artifact." He slides a pouch across the counter.

messages.speaker: Max
messages.text: "Make it three hundred and we leave tonight."

messages.speaker: Ponticius
messages.text: He scowls, then laughs. "Two fifty. Final offer."

messages.speaker: Arin
messages.text: "Take it, Max. We need the coin."

messages.speaker: Max
messages.text: "Deal." I take the pouch.

responses: In the rain-lashed abandoned mill, Lady Ashworth accused Max of being followed despite her demand that he come alone. Max denied it and asked what she had for him, and she handed him a sealed letter proving the governor ordered the fire, warning him to guard it with his life.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: Rain hammers the roof of the abandoned mill. Somewhere below, the wheel groans in the flood.

messages.speaker: Lady Ashworth
messages.text: "You were followed. I told you to come alone."

messages.speaker: Max
messages.text: "Nobody followed me. What do you have for me?"

messages.speaker: Lady Ashworth
messages.text: She hands over a sealed letter. "Proof that the governor ordered the fire. Guard it with your life."

responses: Max knelt by the fallen guard and found iron keys and a duty roster. Vex warned the next patrol was in ten minutes, so Max freed the prisoner, a thin old man who whispered the name Corvin.

messages.speaker: Max
messages.text: I kneel by the fallen guard and check his pockets.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: You find a ring of iron keys and a folded duty roster.

messages.speaker: Vex
messages.text: "The roster says the next patrol is in ten minutes. Move."

messages.speaker: Max
messages.text: I unlock the cell door and pull the prisoner out.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text: The prisoner, a thin old man, clutches your arm and whispers a name: Corvin.

responses: Arin told Max that he did not trust the ferryman because he had lied about the map. Max replied that they would watch him since they still needed his boat. Oskar pushed off from the bank without a word, and the reeds closed behind the boat.

messages.speaker: Arin
messages.text: "I don't trust him. He lied about the map."

messages.speaker: Max
messages.text: "Then we watch him. We still need his boat."

messages.speaker: Oskar
messages.text: The ferryman pushes off from the bank without a word. The reeds close behind the boat.
